The whole 146 hours that I've played this game, I loved it. Persona 3 Reload is an absolute masterpiece. The story is deep but easy to understand, there are no plot holes, the characters are really emotional, and the ending really got to me. I'm going to buy episode Aigis soon. I tried so hard to get into this game. The art is beautiful. The mystery of the dark hour is super intriguing. I would love to get to know the characters. But every single time I hit the dungeon crawling part of the game for the first time I just bounce of from sheer boredom. The dungeons design is the most uninspired thing I've ever seen. Literally the same room copied and pasted over and over again for hours. On top of that the combat is absolutely brain dead. After doing this for an hour nonstop without any engaging content whatsoever I just gave up. Maybe there is a great game hidden in here but I'm simply not willing to waste hours of my life to get to it.

Absolute peak gaming and story telling. Please play this if you have any interest in the slightest.

And the Aigis DLC is also amazing. It's a shame that it also becomes repetitive because it's basically just fighting, but the story parts are amazing. €35 is definitely too much for a DLC though. Buy it when it's on sale and that's it, problem solved. 9/10

Never in my life did I expect to play a game that unironically uses the phrase "The power of friendship" and it wouldn't immediately make me cringe.

There's a lot of stories out there answer the question of "What's the meaning of life?" with "Bonds and relationships", but very few actually manage to stir any emotion out of me in the process. Throw in a little existential dread and bleak undertones of impending doom, and you've got yourself a fun game... and maybe a therapy appointment. A bit ironic though that a game all about the importance of what little time we have in our lives takes over 100 hours to complete its central story.

If you want a short answer, this game is good and I highly recommend it.

The long answer is that just, this game from a story prespective is really emotional and heartbreaking, from the hopeful ties that you experience during the early-game, to the shocks and reveals of the mid-game, and the nihilism this game protrays throughout the entire game. It really gets you into this feeling of hopelessness, like everythings going downhill and you can't control it. But it's also really heartwarming with the bonds you create throughout your social links and everyday life in school. 
Throughout the modern Persona games, this is the darkest but probably the most emotional out of the entire modern trilogy, and I cannot recommend it enough to grab a copy on sale. 
If you love JRPG's and like the dark tones of morality and nihilism, then get this game, you won't regret it.

I said it after P4G, P5, P5S, P5R, and I'll say it again, holy ****. I doubt the Persona series will ever disappoint. Interesting stories, amazing character depth, and just the right amount of challenge to make the games worth their long journeys. If you haven't played a Persona game and you don't care about going in order, I'd start with P5R. If you have played other Persona games and know what to expect, get going on this one, you won't regret it! :)

I hate that P3 fans were right all along.

Climbing tartarus gets pretty tedious and one thing I miss from successive games is how the timed bosses were more tied to a certain story event. P5's handcrafted dungeons were great and in P4 every timed boss was a rescue mission with emotional stakes.

P3's ending though? Not only the best out of the 3 modern persona games, quite possibly the biggest impact an ending has left me in a video game. Whatever lulls and gripes I had before that point feels so insignificant. I've lost sleep over the past 2 nights listening kimi no kioku until my heart can't take it.

I'm apprehensive about replaying games as long as Persona games are, but I have zero doubt I will be replaying this sooner or later. It's already been a battle to not start again, I need to keep at least some semblance of life together.

This game is absolutely amazing.

The characters are so well written and getting to spend time with them over social links is really fun (some of the social links i didn't enjoy but the good ones make up for it!) The fighting is fun too, i did find that after a while it got a bit repetitive though, but the story is my favourite part!! The story is so good tho, it's teaching that (this is just the moral, it doesn't spoil the game but i'll hide just in case) you should enjoy the little things in life, like spending time with friends and having little hobbies because that's what gives life meaning, which i think is really sweet.

Also, i highly advise for new players not to search up stuff about the game because you're very likely to get some spoilers unfortunately! :')

Was afraid of the amount of time I would have to put into this game to complete. After a pretty length 83.3 hours of gameplay, I can say this is the best game I have ever played in my life. The characters are extremely attachable and you'll definitely miss them upon beating the game(not saying they die but they're so well written and relatable you'll miss them). This game also changed my perspective on life. Never thought a video game could do that but it did. If you're into dungeon crawlers, action RPG's, as well as games pretty heavy on its story, you'll love this game. I highly recommend it if so.

The ability to frequently save makes it great with limited playtime. I'm usually able to get through a few levels of the dungeons, as well as a week or two of the school sim. Story is interesting so far! Hoping to beat it by September!

a generally competent remake of a great game. persona 3's gameplay has always been on the iffy side compared to later entries, and they make an attempt here at bridging the gap. some elements are greatly improved, others... eh. likewise, while the game is overall much more visually modern, it loses a lot of the charm of the original in places, with some parts being, in my opinion, quite noticeably downgraded. I think reload's experience is overall an upgrade, but with caveats and asterisks. at the end of the day, persona 3 is a great game, and what version you play to experience the story doesn't matter all that much, and reload is definitely the most accessible version we have.

Persona 3 Reload's gameplay is great with the new graphics of the Unreal Engine. Gameplay wise, combat is fun and quality of life has been improved from the original Persona 3. There are many things to do when you're not in Tartarus, however, definitely take your time when playing this game as Tartarus can be a bit repetitive. What makes the game truly shine is the emotional depth of the story throughout the game. Highly recommend this game for people who have played any other Persona series before, if this is your first, I think this is a good entry but I think there may be other Persona games that will provide you a better experience when getting into the series.

The music and artworks are amazing, i love it so muchhhh 💖 And the storyline is as good as i remember. In fact now that I'm older i can understand what's going on even better. I've played persona 4 and 5 too, but really from all of the persona series i've played persona 3 really have a special place in my heart 🌟

In comparison to the next entry to the series Persona 4 Golden (P4G), the story is slow paced and the characters aren't established friends at the start. Giving you a more serious cast than the gag-filled P4G ensemble, the biggest thorn for the casual fan would be the Tartarus segments as if you're not a big fan of the core gameplay of the series and are more into the story, it will be a slogfest for you to progress.

I've had my fair share of feeling that the gameplay loop is like a chore after 100+ hours since the night time part is lacking social link related activities but overall I enjoyed my time playing, specially the music.

The graphics and visuals are a big upgrade though that's a plus as someone who haven't played the original trio games (P3, P3P and P3FES).
Great game, the pacing is a bit slow at the start, almost in a "whats the point" way but soon it picks up, great fun for a few hours a day!
